info.name: Ding Platform Backend - Full API
info.description: Complete backend collection (Auth, User, Social, Profile, Posts, Feed, Privacy, Likes, Comments, Chat, Noro, Moderation, Marketplace).

item.name: Health

request.description: Sends a GET request to the API root (`{{baseUrl}}`). This is the simplest possible liveness check — if the server responds, the API is reachable. No authentication or parameters are required. Returns a basic welcome or status message confirming the API is online. Useful for smoke tests and uptime monitors.

Returns a structured health status for the Ding Platform Backend. No authentication is required. The response includes the overall service status and may include sub-system checks (e.g., database, cache). Use this endpoint in monitoring dashboards and automated health checks to detect outages or degraded performance.

item.description: The Health folder contains endpoints for verifying that the Ding Platform Backend API is up and running. These requests are used by DevOps engineers, monitoring tools, and automated uptime checks to confirm the server is reachable and responding correctly. The App Root endpoint confirms the API is live, while the Health Check endpoint provides a structured status response indicating service health.

item.name: Authentication

request.description: Registers a new user account on the Ding platform. Accepts a JSON body with `email`, `password`, and `name`. On success, the account is created and an email verification OTP is sent to the provided address. Returns the newly created user object. The account must be verified via the Verify Email endpoint before it can be used to log in.

response.name: Created - 201
response.body: {"success": true, "message": "Account created successfully. Please verify your email.", "data": {"id": "64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1", "name": "Alex Johnson", "email": "alex.johnson@example.com", "isVerified": false, "createdAt": "2024-06-15T10:30:00.000Z"}}

exec: if (pm.response.code===200){const d=pm.response.json().data; pm.collectionVariables.set("accessToken", d.accessToken); pm.collectionVariables.set("userToken", d.accessToken); if (d.user?.id) pm.collectionVariables.set("userId", d.user.id);}

request.description: Authenticates an existing user with their `email` and `password`. On success, returns an `accessToken` (Bearer JWT) and the authenticated user's profile. The test script automatically stores the `accessToken` and `userId` as collection variables for use in subsequent authenticated requests. The account must be verified before login is permitted.

Verifies a user's email address using a one-time password (OTP) sent during signup. Accepts a JSON body with `email` and `otp`. On success, the account is marked as verified and the user can proceed to log in. Returns a confirmation message. The OTP is typically 6 digits and expires after a short window.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "message": "Email verified successfully. You can now log in.", "data": {"id": "64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1", "email": "alex.johnson@example.com", "isVerified": true}}

request.description: Resends the email verification OTP to the specified email address. Accepts a JSON body with `email`. Use this when the original OTP has expired or was not received. Returns a confirmation that the OTP has been re-sent. No authentication is required.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "message": "Verification OTP has been resent to alex.johnson@example.com. Please check your inbox."}

request.description: Initiates the forgot-password flow by sending a password-reset OTP to the user's registered email address. Accepts a JSON body with `email`. No authentication is required. After calling this endpoint, the user should use the Verify Forgot Password endpoint to confirm the OTP before resetting their password.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "message": "A password reset OTP has been sent to alex.johnson@example.com. It will expire in 10 minutes."}

request.description: Verifies the OTP sent during the forgot-password flow. Accepts a JSON body with `email` and `otp`. On success, the OTP is validated and the user is authorized to set a new password via the Reset Password endpoint. This is the second step in the three-step password recovery flow.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "message": "OTP verified successfully. You may now reset your password."}

request.description: Sets a new password for a user who has completed the forgot-password OTP verification flow. Accepts a JSON body with `email` and `newPassword`. No authentication token is required, but the OTP must have been verified first. On success, the password is updated and the user can log in with the new credentials.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "message": "Password has been reset successfully. You can now log in with your new password."}

request.description: Allows an authenticated user to change their current password. Requires a Bearer token. Accepts a JSON body with `oldPassword` (the current password for verification) and `newPassword` (the desired new password). Returns a success confirmation. Use this for in-app password change flows where the user is already logged in.

Issues a new access token using a valid refresh token. This endpoint is used to silently re-authenticate users whose access token has expired, without requiring them to log in again. The refresh token is typically sent via an HTTP-only cookie or request body. Returns a new `accessToken` on success.

Returns the profile of the currently authenticated user. Requires a Bearer token. No path parameters or query parameters are needed — the user is identified from the token. Returns the full user object including ID, name, email, profile picture, and account metadata. Useful for populating profile pages and verifying token validity.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "data": {"id": "64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1", "name": "Alex Johnson", "email": "alex.johnson@example.com", "username": "alexj", "bio": "Living life one ding at a time 🔔", "profilePicture": "https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/alexj.jpg", "isVerified": true, "isActive": true, "role": "user", "createdAt": "2024-06-15T10:30:00.000Z", "updatedAt": "2024-06-20T08:15:00.000Z"}}

request.description: Logs out the currently authenticated user by invalidating the current session's access token. Requires a Bearer token. After calling this endpoint, the token is no longer valid and subsequent requests using it will be rejected. Use this for single-device logout (e.g., when the user taps "Log Out" in the app).

Logs out the authenticated user from all active sessions across all devices. Requires a Bearer token. All tokens associated with the user's account are invalidated. Use this for security-sensitive actions such as "Log out everywhere" after a suspected account compromise.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "message": "Logged out from all devices successfully. 3 sessions terminated."}

item.description: The Authentication folder covers all identity and access management flows for the Ding platform. It includes user registration, email verification, login, password management (forgot/reset/update), token refresh, and session termination. Most endpoints are unauthenticated (used during onboarding), while password update, logout, and token refresh require a valid Bearer token. Developers integrating with Ding should start here to obtain an access token before calling any protected endpoints.

item.name: Users

request.description: Toggles the active/inactive status of a specific user account. The `userId` path variable identifies the user. When deactivated, the user loses access to the platform. When reactivated, access is restored. Typically used by administrators for account management. Requires a Bearer token with admin privileges. Returns the updated user object with the new activity status.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "message": "User activity status updated.", "data": {"id": "64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1", "name": "Alex Johnson", "email": "alex.johnson@example.com", "isActive": false, "updatedAt": "2024-06-21T14:00:00.000Z"}}

request.description: Permanently deletes a user account from the Ding platform. Requires an admin-level Bearer token. The `targetUserId` path variable identifies the account to delete. This action is irreversible and removes all associated user data. Intended for use by platform administrators handling account removal requests or policy violations.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "message": "User account has been permanently deleted.", "data": {"deletedUserId": "64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1"}}

item.description: The Users folder contains administrative endpoints for managing user accounts on the Ding platform. These operations require an admin-level Bearer token and are intended for platform administrators and moderation tools. Admins can toggle a user's active status (e.g., suspend or reactivate an account) or permanently delete a user by their target user ID.

item.name: Social

request.description: Retrieves all pending friend requests for the authenticated user. Requires a Bearer token. Returns a list of incoming friend requests, each containing the sender's user profile and the timestamp of the request. Use this to populate the "Friend Requests" inbox in the app.

Returns the full list of friends for the authenticated user. Requires a Bearer token. Each entry in the response includes the friend's user profile and the date the friendship was established. Use this to render the user's friends list in the app.

Sends a friend request to another user identified by `targetUserId` in the URL path. Requires a Bearer token. The target user will receive a notification and can accept or reject the request. Returns a confirmation of the sent request. A user cannot send a request to someone they are already friends with or have already sent a pending request to.

Accepts a pending friend request from the user identified by `targetUserId`. Requires a Bearer token. Once accepted, both users are added to each other's friends list and a friendship record is created. Returns a confirmation of the accepted friendship. The `targetUserId` must have a pending outgoing request to the authenticated user.

Rejects a pending friend request from the user identified by `targetUserId`. Requires a Bearer token. The request is removed and no friendship is created. The sender is not notified of the rejection. Returns a confirmation that the request was declined.

Removes an existing friendship between the authenticated user and the user identified by `targetUserId`. Requires a Bearer token. Both users are removed from each other's friends list. This action does not block the other user. Returns a confirmation of the removal.

Follows the user identified by `targetUserId`. Requires a Bearer token. Following is a one-directional relationship — the authenticated user will see the target user's content in their feed. Returns a confirmation of the follow action. If the target user has a private account, a follow request may be created instead.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "message": "You are now following this user.", "data": {"followedUser": {"id": "64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d5", "name": "Sofia Nguyen", "username": "sofiang", "profilePicture": "https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/sofiang.jpg"}, "followedAt": "2024-06-21T16:00:00.000Z"}}

request.description: Unfollows the user identified by `targetUserId`. Requires a Bearer token. The authenticated user will no longer see the target user's content in their feed. The target user is not notified. Returns a confirmation of the unfollow action.

Returns the list of users who follow the authenticated user. Requires a Bearer token. Each entry includes the follower's user profile and the date they started following. Use this to render the "Followers" list on a user's profile page.

Returns the list of users that the authenticated user is following. Requires a Bearer token. Each entry includes the followed user's profile and the date the follow was initiated. Use this to render the "Following" list on a user's profile page.

Returns a personalized list of suggested users to add as friends. Requires a Bearer token. Recommendations are based on mutual connections, shared interests, or platform activity. Use this to power the "People You May Know" feature in the app.

Returns a personalized list of suggested users to follow. Requires a Bearer token. Recommendations are based on the user's existing social graph, content preferences, and trending accounts. Use this to power the "Suggested for You" or "Discover" section of the app.

Returns a summary of the authenticated user's social statistics. Requires a Bearer token. The response includes counts for friends, followers, following, blocked users, and muted users. Use this to populate the stats section of a user's profile page.

Returns the list of users who are mutual friends between the authenticated user and the user identified by `targetUserId`. Requires a Bearer token. Mutual friends are users who appear in both users' friends lists. Use this to display shared connections on another user's profile page.

Blocks the user identified by `targetUserId`. Requires a Bearer token. Blocking prevents the target user from viewing the authenticated user's profile, sending messages, or interacting with their content. Any existing friendship or follow relationship is also removed. Returns a confirmation of the block action.

Unblocks the user identified by `targetUserId`. Requires a Bearer token. After unblocking, the target user can interact with the authenticated user's content again, though any previously removed friendships or follows are not automatically restored. Returns a confirmation of the unblock action.

Returns the list of users that the authenticated user has blocked. Requires a Bearer token. Each entry includes the blocked user's profile and the date they were blocked. Use this to populate the "Blocked Users" section in the app's privacy settings.

Mutes the user identified by `targetUserId`. Requires a Bearer token. Muting hides the target user's posts and activity from the authenticated user's feed without removing the friendship or follow relationship. The muted user is not notified. Returns a confirmation of the mute action.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "message": "User has been muted. Their posts will no longer appear in your feed.", "data": {"mutedUser": {"id": "64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d7", "name": "Lena Müller", "username": "lenam"}, "mutedAt": "2024-06-21T18:00:00.000Z"}}

request.description: Unmutes the user identified by `targetUserId`. Requires a Bearer token. After unmuting, the target user's posts and activity will reappear in the authenticated user's feed. Returns a confirmation of the unmute action.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "message": "User has been unmuted. Their posts will now appear in your feed again."}

request.description: Returns the list of users that the authenticated user has muted. Requires a Bearer token. Each entry includes the muted user's profile and the date they were muted. Use this to populate the "Muted Users" section in the app's settings.

item.description: The Social folder covers the full social graph of the Ding platform, including friend management, follow/unfollow relationships, blocking, muting, and discovery features. Authenticated users can send, accept, and reject friend requests, follow or unfollow other users, view their followers and following lists, block or mute users to control their experience, and get personalized friend and follow recommendations. Social stats provide a summary of a user's connections. All endpoints require a valid Bearer token.

item.name: Notifications

request.description: Retrieves all notifications for the authenticated user. Requires a Bearer token. Returns a paginated list of notification objects, each containing the notification type (e.g., friend request, like, comment, follow), the triggering user's profile, a message, and a read/unread status. Use this to populate the notification feed in the app.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "data": [{"id": "notif_001", "type": "friend_request", "message": "Maria Garcia sent you a friend request.", "actor": {"id": "64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d2", "name": "Maria Garcia", "username": "mariagg", "profilePicture": "https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/mariagg.jpg"}, "read": false, "createdAt": "2024-06-21T09:00:00.000Z"}, {"id": "notif_002", "type": "like", "message": "James Lee liked your post.", "actor": {"id": "64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d3", "name": "James Lee", "username": "jameslee", "profilePicture": "https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/jameslee.jpg"}, "read": true, "createdAt": "2024-06-20T14:30:00.000Z"}], "total": 2, "unreadCount": 1}}

request.description: Returns the count of unread notifications for the authenticated user. Requires a Bearer token. Use this to power the notification badge (red dot/number) displayed on the notification icon in the app's navigation bar. The response is a lightweight count object, not the full notification list.

Marks a single notification as read. Requires a Bearer token. The `messageId` path variable identifies the specific notification to mark. Returns the updated notification object with `read: true`. Use this when a user taps on an individual notification in the app.

Marks all of the authenticated user's notifications as read in a single operation. Requires a Bearer token. Returns a confirmation with the number of notifications updated. Use this for the "Mark all as read" button in the notification center.

item.description: The Notifications folder provides endpoints for retrieving and managing in-app notifications for authenticated Ding users. Users can fetch their full notification list, check the count of unread notifications, mark a single notification as read by its ID, or mark all notifications as read at once. These endpoints are typically consumed by the frontend to power notification badges and feeds. All requests require a valid Bearer token.

item.name: Sessions

request.description: Returns all active login sessions for the authenticated user. Requires a Bearer token. Each session object includes the device type, operating system, IP address, location, and the date the session was created. Use this to power the "Active Sessions" or "Where You're Logged In" screen in the app's security settings.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success": true, "data": [{"id": "sess_001", "device": "iPhone 15 Pro", "os": "iOS 17.4", "browser": "Ding App", "ipAddress": "192.168.1.42", "location": "Lagos, Nigeria", "isCurrent": true, "createdAt": "2024-06-21T08:00:00.000Z"}, {"id": "sess_002", "device": "MacBook Pro", "os": "macOS 14.4", "browser": "Chrome 125", "ipAddress": "192.168.1.10", "location": "Lagos, Nigeria", "isCurrent": false, "createdAt": "2024-06-19T20:30:00.000Z"}], "total": 2}}

item.description: The Sessions folder provides endpoints for managing active login sessions for the authenticated user. Users can retrieve a list of all their current sessions, including device and location metadata, which is useful for security auditing and allowing users to review where their account is logged in. All requests require a valid Bearer token.

item.name: Profile

request.description: Searches for user profiles by a text query string. Returns a paginated list of matching profiles. Use the `query` parameter to specify the search term (e.g., a username or display name), and `page`/`limit` to control pagination. This endpoint does not require authentication and is suitable for public user discovery.

Returns the full profile of the currently authenticated user, including bio, location, website, profile picture URL, cover photo URL, follower/following counts, and privacy settings. Requires a valid Bearer token in the `Authorization` header.

Fetches the public profile of any user by their unique `userId` path variable. Returns profile details such as display name, bio, avatar, cover photo, and follower/following counts. This endpoint is publicly accessible and does not require authentication.

Creates or updates the authenticated user's profile. Accepts a JSON body with optional fields: `bio` (short description), `location` (city or region), `website` (personal URL), and `phoneNumber` (E.164 format). If a profile already exists it is updated; otherwise a new one is created. Requires a Bearer token.

Uploads or replaces the authenticated user's profile picture. The request body must be `multipart/form-data` with a `file` field containing the image. Returns the updated profile picture URL upon success. Requires a Bearer token.

Uploads or replaces the authenticated user's cover photo (the banner image displayed at the top of their profile page). The request body must be `multipart/form-data` with a `file` field containing the image. Returns the updated cover photo URL upon success. Requires a Bearer token.

Updates the privacy settings stored on the authenticated user's profile. Accepts a JSON body with fields such as `profileVisibility` (`PUBLIC`, `FRIENDS`, `PRIVATE`), `postsVisibility`, `emailVisibility`, and `allowCameraAccess`. Only the fields provided in the request body are updated. Requires a Bearer token.

Permanently deletes the authenticated user's profile and all associated data from the Ding platform. This action is irreversible. Requires a valid Bearer token. Returns a confirmation message upon successful deletion.

item.description: The **Profile** folder covers all endpoints related to user profile management on the Ding platform. This includes searching for other users, retrieving your own or another user's profile, creating or updating profile information (bio, location, website, phone number), uploading a profile picture or cover photo, adjusting profile-level privacy settings, and deleting an account. These endpoints are used by both authenticated users managing their own profiles and by clients displaying public profile pages to other users.

item.name: Posts

request.description: Returns a paginated list of all posts on the platform. Use the `page` and `limit` query parameters to control pagination. This endpoint is publicly accessible and does not require authentication. Each post object includes the content, author info, media URLs, like count, comment count, and creation timestamp.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success":true,"data":{"posts":[{"id":"post_abc123","content":"Just shipped a new feature on Ding! 🎉","mediaUrls":["https://cdn.ding.app/media/post_abc123_img1.jpg"],"privacy":"PUBLIC","author":{"id":"usr_e5f6g7h8","username":"johnny_rivers","avatarUrl":"https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/johnny_rivers.jpg"},"likesCount":42,"commentsCount":7,"createdAt":"2024-03-10T12:00:00Z"},{"id":"post_def456","content":"Beautiful sunset from the rooftop 🌅","mediaUrls":[],"privacy":"PUBLIC","author":{"id":"usr_x9y8z7w6","username":"sara_design","avatarUrl":"https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/sara_design.jpg"},"likesCount":118,"commentsCount":14,"createdAt":"2024-03-09T18:45:00Z"}],"page":1,"limit":10,"total":2}}

request.description: Returns the total number of posts on the platform (or for the authenticated user, depending on server-side logic). Useful for displaying post counts on profile pages or dashboards. This endpoint does not require authentication.

Returns the list of posts that the authenticated user has saved/bookmarked. Useful for building a "Saved" tab in the app. Requires a Bearer token. Each item in the response includes the full post object along with the timestamp when it was saved.

Fetches the full details of a single post identified by the `postId` path variable. Returns the post content, media URLs, author information, privacy setting, like count, comment count, and timestamps. This endpoint is publicly accessible.

response.body: {"success":true,"data":{"id":"post_abc123","content":"Just shipped a new feature on Ding! 🎉","mediaUrls":["https://cdn.ding.app/media/post_abc123_img1.jpg"],"privacy":"PUBLIC","author":{"id":"usr_e5f6g7h8","username":"johnny_rivers","displayName":"Johnny Rivers","avatarUrl":"https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/johnny_rivers.jpg"},"likesCount":42,"commentsCount":7,"isSaved":false,"isLiked":false,"createdAt":"2024-03-10T12:00:00Z","updatedAt":"2024-03-10T12:00:00Z"}}

exec: if (pm.response.code===201 || pm.response.code===200){ const d=pm.response.json().data; if (d?.id) pm.collectionVariables.set("postId", d.id); }

request.description: Creates a new post on behalf of the authenticated user. The JSON body must include `content` (the post text), and optionally `mediaUrls` (an array of media file URLs) and `privacy` (`PUBLIC`, `FRIENDS`, or `PRIVATE`). On success, returns the newly created post object including its generated `id`, which is automatically stored in the `postId` collection variable by the test script. Requires a Bearer token.

response.name: Created - 201
response.body: {"success":true,"message":"Post created successfully","data":{"id":"post_ghi789","content":"Loving the new Ding features! Who else is excited? 🙌","mediaUrls":["https://cdn.ding.app/media/upload_xyz789.jpg"],"privacy":"PUBLIC","author":{"id":"usr_a1b2c3d4","username":"zack_river","avatarUrl":"https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/zack_river.jpg"},"likesCount":0,"commentsCount":0,"createdAt":"2024-03-10T17:00:00Z"}}

request.description: Updates an existing post identified by the `postId` path variable. Accepts a JSON body with the fields to update, such as `content`. Only the authenticated post author can update their own post. Requires a Bearer token.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success":true,"message":"Post updated successfully","data":{"id":"post_ghi789","content":"Loving the new Ding features! Updated with more details 🙌✨","mediaUrls":["https://cdn.ding.app/media/upload_xyz789.jpg"],"privacy":"PUBLIC","updatedAt":"2024-03-10T17:30:00Z"}}

request.description: Toggles the like status of a post for the authenticated user. If the user has not yet liked the post, this call adds a like. If the user has already liked the post, this call removes the like. Returns the updated like state and total like count. Requires a Bearer token.

Toggles the saved/bookmarked status of a post for the authenticated user. If the post is not yet saved, this call saves it. If it is already saved, this call removes it from the user's saved list. Returns the updated save state. Requires a Bearer token.

Returns the edit history of a post identified by the `postId` path variable. Each history entry includes the previous content, the timestamp of the edit, and the editor's user ID. Useful for moderation and transparency features. Requires a Bearer token.

response.body: {"success":true,"data":{"postId":"post_ghi789","history":[{"version":2,"content":"Loving the new Ding features! Updated with more details 🙌✨","editedAt":"2024-03-10T17:30:00Z","editedBy":"usr_a1b2c3d4"},{"version":1,"content":"Loving the new Ding features! Who else is excited? 🙌","editedAt":"2024-03-10T17:00:00Z","editedBy":"usr_a1b2c3d4"}]}}

request.description: Adds a new comment to the post identified by the `postId` path variable. The JSON body must include a `content` field with the comment text. Returns the newly created comment object including its `id`, author info, and timestamp. Requires a Bearer token.

Retrieves all comments for the post identified by the `postId` path variable. Returns an array of comment objects, each containing the comment text, author info, like count, reply count, and creation timestamp. This endpoint is publicly accessible and does not require authentication.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success":true,"data":{"comments":[{"id":"cmt_001xyz","content":"This is amazing, congrats on shipping! 🔥","author":{"id":"usr_a1b2c3d4","username":"zack_river","avatarUrl":"https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/zack_river.jpg"},"likesCount":3,"repliesCount":1,"createdAt":"2024-03-10T18:10:00Z"},{"id":"cmt_002abc","content":"Can't wait to try this out!","author":{"id":"usr_x9y8z7w6","username":"sara_design","avatarUrl":"https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/sara_design.jpg"},"likesCount":1,"repliesCount":0,"createdAt":"2024-03-10T18:15:00Z"}],"total":2}}

request.description: Returns the list of users who have liked the post identified by the `postId` path variable. Each entry includes the user's ID, display name, and avatar URL. This endpoint is publicly accessible and does not require authentication.

Permanently deletes a comment identified by the `commentId` path variable from a post. Only the comment author or a moderator can delete a comment. Returns a confirmation message upon success. Requires a Bearer token.

Permanently deletes the post identified by the `postId` path variable. Only the post author can delete their own post. This action also removes all associated likes, comments, and saved references. Returns a confirmation message upon success. Requires a Bearer token.

item.description: The **Posts** folder covers the full lifecycle of posts on the Ding platform. It includes endpoints for listing, counting, creating, updating, and deleting posts, as well as fetching a single post by ID, retrieving a post's edit history, saving/unsaving posts for later, toggling likes, and managing comments directly on a post. Some endpoints are public (no auth required) while write operations require a Bearer token. The `postId` path variable is used throughout to identify the target post.

item.name: Feed

request.description: Retrieves a paginated list of posts for the authenticated user's feed. The `type` query parameter controls the feed variant — `HOME` returns posts from followed users, while `EXPLORE` returns trending or recommended content. Use `page` and `limit` for pagination. Requires a Bearer token.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success":true,"data":{"posts":[{"id":"post_abc123","content":"Just shipped a new feature on Ding! 🎉","mediaUrls":["https://cdn.ding.app/media/post_abc123_img1.jpg"],"privacy":"PUBLIC","author":{"id":"usr_e5f6g7h8","username":"johnny_rivers","avatarUrl":"https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/johnny_rivers.jpg"},"likesCount":42,"commentsCount":7,"isSaved":false,"isLiked":true,"createdAt":"2024-03-10T12:00:00Z"},{"id":"post_def456","content":"Beautiful sunset from the rooftop 🌅","mediaUrls":["https://cdn.ding.app/media/post_def456_img1.jpg"],"privacy":"PUBLIC","author":{"id":"usr_x9y8z7w6","username":"sara_design","avatarUrl":"https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/sara_design.jpg"},"likesCount":118,"commentsCount":14,"isSaved":true,"isLiked":false,"createdAt":"2024-03-10T09:30:00Z"}],"page":1,"limit":20,"total":2}}

item.description: The **Feed** folder contains the endpoint responsible for fetching a user's personalized content feed on Ding. The feed can be filtered by type (e.g., `HOME`, `EXPLORE`) and supports pagination via `page` and `limit` query parameters. This endpoint is used by the main app screen to display posts, reels, and other content from followed users and recommended accounts. A valid Bearer token is required.

item.name: Privacy

request.description: Retrieves the current privacy settings for the authenticated user. Returns a JSON object indicating which pieces of information (email, phone number, etc.) are visible to other users. Requires a Bearer token.

Updates the authenticated user's global privacy preferences. Accepts a JSON body with boolean fields such as `showEmail` and `showPhone`. Only the fields included in the request body are modified; omitted fields retain their current values. Requires a Bearer token.

item.description: The **Privacy** folder contains endpoints for reading and updating a user's global privacy preferences on Ding. These settings control the visibility of sensitive information such as email address and phone number. Authenticated users can retrieve their current privacy configuration or patch individual settings. These endpoints are typically accessed from the account settings screen of the Ding app.

item.name: Likes

request.description: Adds a like to the post identified by the `postId` path variable on behalf of the authenticated user. Unlike the toggle endpoint in the Posts folder, this is an explicit like action — calling it when the post is already liked may return an error or be idempotent depending on server behavior. Requires a Bearer token.

Removes the authenticated user's like from the post identified by the `postId` path variable. This is an explicit unlike action. If the user has not liked the post, the server may return an error or handle it gracefully. Requires a Bearer token.
Adds a like to the comment identified by the `commentId` path variable on behalf of the authenticated user. Returns the updated like count for the comment. Requires a Bearer token.
Removes the authenticated user's like from the comment identified by the `commentId` path variable. Returns the updated like count for the comment. Requires a Bearer token.

Returns the list of users who have liked the post identified by the `postId` path variable. Each entry includes the user's ID, display name, and avatar URL. This endpoint is publicly accessible and does not require authentication.

item.description: The **Likes** folder provides dedicated endpoints for liking and unliking both posts and comments on Ding. These endpoints are separate from the toggle-based like action found in the Posts folder and offer explicit `POST` (like) and `DELETE` (unlike) semantics. A `GET` endpoint is also available to retrieve the full list of users who liked a specific post. All write operations require a Bearer token, while the read endpoint is public.

item.name: Comments

request.description: Creates a new comment on the post identified by the `postId` path variable. The JSON body must include a `content` field with the comment text. Returns the newly created comment object including its `id`, author details, and creation timestamp. Requires a Bearer token.

Retrieves all top-level comments for the post identified by the `postId` path variable. Returns an array of comment objects with author info, content, like count, reply count, and timestamps. This endpoint is publicly accessible and does not require authentication.

Really enjoyed reading this 👏","author":{"id":"usr_a1b2c3d4","username":"zack_river","avatarUrl":"https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/zack_river.jpg"},"likesCount":5,"repliesCount":2,"createdAt":"2024-03-10T20:15:00Z"},{"id":"cmt_002abc","content":"Can't wait to try this out!","author":{"id":"usr_x9y8z7w6","username":"sara_design","avatarUrl":"https://cdn.ding.app/avatars/sara_design.jpg"},"likesCount":1,"repliesCount":0,"createdAt":"2024-03-10T18:15:00Z"}],"total":2}}

request.description: Fetches all replies to the comment identified by the `commentId` path variable. Returns a threaded list of reply objects, each containing the reply text, author info, like count, and timestamp. This endpoint is publicly accessible and does not require authentication.

Updates the text content of the comment identified by the `commentId` path variable. The JSON body must include a `content` field with the new comment text. Only the comment author can edit their own comment. Returns the updated comment object. Requires a Bearer token.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"success":true,"message":"Comment updated","data":{"id":"cmt_003def","content":"Great post! Really enjoyed reading this — highly recommend 👏","updatedAt":"2024-03-10T21:00:00Z"}}

request.description: Permanently deletes the comment identified by the `commentId` path variable. Only the comment author or a moderator can perform this action. Returns a confirmation message upon success. Requires a Bearer token.

item.description: The **Comments** folder contains the dedicated comments module for the Ding platform, providing endpoints to create, read, update, and delete comments on posts, as well as fetch threaded replies to a specific comment. This module mirrors some functionality found in the Posts folder but operates under the `/comments` route namespace. The `commentId` and `postId` path variables are used to target specific resources. Write operations require a Bearer token; read endpoints are public.

item.name: Chat

request.description: Creates a new chat room. The request body must include a `name` (string) and a `type` field — typically `"GROUP"` for a named group room or `"DIRECT"` for a one-on-one room. Requires a Bearer token. Returns the newly created room object including its ID, name, type, creator, and creation timestamp.

Creates or retrieves an existing direct (one-on-one) chat room between the authenticated user and a target user. The request body must include `targetUserId` — the ID of the other participant. If a direct room already exists between the two users, the existing room is returned instead of creating a duplicate. Requires a Bearer token.

Creates a new group chat room with a specified name and an initial list of member IDs. The request body must include `name` (string) and `memberIds` (array of user ID strings). The authenticated user is automatically added as the room owner. Requires a Bearer token. Returns the created group room object with its ID, name, member list, and metadata.

Returns a list of all chat rooms the authenticated user is a member of, including both direct and group rooms. Each room object includes the room ID, name, type, last message preview, unread count, and participant metadata. Requires a Bearer token. Supports pagination via optional `page` and `limit` query parameters.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"data":[{"id":"room_grp_7c3d9e1f","name":"Engineering","type":"GROUP","unreadCount":3,"lastMessage":{"content":"Hey team, standup in 5!","senderId":"user_xyz789","sentAt":"2024-06-01T09:55:00Z"},"memberCount":3,"updatedAt":"2024-06-01T09:55:00Z"},{"id":"room_dm_4e7f1a2b","name":null,"type":"DIRECT","unreadCount":0,"lastMessage":{"content":"Sounds good, see you then!","senderId":"user_abc123","sentAt":"2024-05-31T18:20:00Z"},"memberCount":2,"updatedAt":"2024-05-31T18:20:00Z"}],"pagination":{"page":1,"limit":20,"total":2}}

request.description: Retrieves the full details of a specific chat room by its ID. The `roomId` path variable identifies the room. Returns the room's name, type, member list with roles, creation date, and the most recent message. The authenticated user must be a member of the room. Requires a Bearer token.

Updates the metadata of an existing chat room. Currently supports updating the room `name`. The `roomId` path variable identifies the room to update. Only room admins or the room owner can perform this action. Requires a Bearer token. Returns the updated room object.

Allows the authenticated user to leave a chat room they are currently a member of. The `roomId` path variable identifies the room. If the user is the last member or the owner, additional cleanup logic may apply. Requires a Bearer token. Returns a success confirmation upon leaving.

Adds one or more users to an existing group chat room. The request body must include `memberIds` — an array of user ID strings to add. The `roomId` path variable identifies the target room. Only room admins or the owner can add members. Requires a Bearer token. Returns the updated member list.

Removes a specific member from a group chat room. The `roomId` path variable identifies the room and `targetUserId` identifies the member to remove. Only room admins or the owner can remove members. Requires a Bearer token. Returns a success confirmation.

Updates the role of a specific member within a group chat room. The `roomId` and `targetUserId` path variables identify the room and the member. The request body must include `role` — valid values are typically `"ADMIN"` or `"MEMBER"`. Only the room owner can change member roles. Requires a Bearer token. Returns the updated member object.

Updates the per-room notification settings for the authenticated user. The `roomId` path variable identifies the room. The request body supports `muteNotifications` (boolean) — set to `true` to silence notifications for this room, or `false` to re-enable them. Requires a Bearer token. Returns the updated settings object.

Retrieves a paginated list of messages in a specific chat room. The `roomId` path variable identifies the room. Supports `page` and `limit` query parameters for pagination (defaults: page=1, limit=20). Messages are returned in reverse-chronological order. Each message object includes the sender, content, timestamp, reactions, and read status. Requires a Bearer token.

Sends a new text message to a specific chat room. The `roomId` path variable identifies the destination room. The request body must include `content` (string) — the text of the message. Requires a Bearer token. Returns the created message object including its ID, sender, content, and timestamp.

Sends a message with a media attachment (image, video, or file) to a specific chat room. The request uses `multipart/form-data`. The `file` field contains the binary file to upload, and the optional `content` field provides an accompanying text caption. The `roomId` path variable identifies the destination room. Requires a Bearer token. Returns the created message object with a URL to the uploaded media.

Retrieves the full details of a single chat message by its ID. The `messageId` path variable identifies the message. Returns the message content, sender, timestamp, reactions, read receipts, and whether the message has been edited or deleted. The authenticated user must be a member of the room the message belongs to. Requires a Bearer token.

Edits the text content of an existing chat message. The `messageId` path variable identifies the message to update. The request body must include `content` (string) — the new text. Only the original sender of the message can edit it. Requires a Bearer token. Returns the updated message object with an `isEdited` flag set to `true`.

Deletes a specific chat message by its ID. The `messageId` path variable identifies the message to delete. Only the original sender or a room admin can delete a message. Requires a Bearer token. The message may be soft-deleted (marked as deleted) rather than permanently removed, depending on platform policy. Returns a success confirmation.

Forwards an existing message to one or more chat rooms. The request body must include `messageId` (the ID of the message to forward) and `roomIds` (an array of destination room IDs). The authenticated user must be a member of all destination rooms. Requires a Bearer token. Returns a list of the newly created forwarded message objects in each target room.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"data":{"forwardedMessages":[{"id":"msg_fwd_a1b2","roomId":"room_dm_4e7f1a2b","originalMessageId":"msg_3f4e5d","content":"Hey team, standup in 5!","forwardedBy":"user_abc123","sentAt":"2024-06-02T11:15:00Z"},{"id":"msg_fwd_c3d4","roomId":"room_grp_7c3d9e1f","originalMessageId":"msg_3f4e5d","content":"Hey team, standup in 5!","forwardedBy":"user_abc123","sentAt":"2024-06-02T11:15:00Z"}]}}

request.description: Retrieves the edit history of a specific chat message. The `messageId` path variable identifies the message. Returns an ordered list of previous versions of the message content, each with the timestamp of the edit. Useful for auditing message changes. Requires a Bearer token and membership in the room the message belongs to.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"data":{"messageId":"msg_9a8b7c","editHistory":[{"version":1,"content":"Hey everyone, the build is green!","editedAt":"2024-06-02T11:00:00Z"},{"version":2,"content":"Hey everyone, the build is green! ✅","editedAt":"2024-06-02T11:02:00Z"}]}}

request.description: Adds an emoji reaction to a specific chat message. The `messageId` path variable identifies the message. The request body must include `emoji` (string) — the Unicode emoji character to react with (e.g., `"👍"`). Requires a Bearer token. Returns the updated reaction summary for the message, including counts per emoji.

Removes a specific emoji reaction from a chat message. The `messageId` path variable identifies the message, and the emoji is URL-encoded in the path (e.g., `%F0%9F%91%8D` for 👍). Only the user who originally added the reaction can remove it. Requires a Bearer token. Returns the updated reaction summary for the message.

Toggles an emoji reaction on a chat message — adds the reaction if the user has not yet reacted with that emoji, or removes it if they have. The `messageId` path variable identifies the message. The request body must include `emoji` (string). Requires a Bearer token. Returns the updated reaction state indicating whether the reaction was added or removed.

Retrieves all emoji reactions for a specific chat message. The `messageId` path variable identifies the message. Returns a grouped summary of reactions, including the emoji, the total count, and the list of users who reacted with each emoji. Requires a Bearer token and membership in the room the message belongs to.

Marks a specific chat message as read by the authenticated user. The `messageId` path variable identifies the message. This updates the read receipt for that message and may affect the unread count for the room. Requires a Bearer token. Returns a success confirmation with the updated read timestamp.

Marks all unread messages in a specific chat room as read for the authenticated user. The `roomId` path variable identifies the room. This is a bulk read operation that resets the unread count for the room to zero. Requires a Bearer token. Returns a success confirmation.

Returns the number of unread messages in a specific chat room for the authenticated user. The `roomId` path variable identifies the room. Useful for displaying badge counts in the chat UI. Requires a Bearer token. Returns an object with the `unreadCount` field.

Returns the unread message counts across all chat rooms the authenticated user is a member of. Each entry in the response includes the room ID and its corresponding unread count. Useful for rendering notification badges on the chat room list. Requires a Bearer token.

Pins a specific message in a chat room so it is prominently visible to all members. The `roomId` and `messageId` path variables identify the room and the message to pin. Only room admins or the owner can pin messages. Requires a Bearer token. Returns a success confirmation with the pinned message details.

Removes the pinned status from a specific message in a chat room. The `roomId` and `messageId` path variables identify the room and the message to unpin. Only room admins or the owner can unpin messages. Requires a Bearer token. Returns a success confirmation.

Retrieves all currently pinned messages in a specific chat room. The `roomId` path variable identifies the room. Returns an array of pinned message objects, each including the message content, sender, timestamp, and the user who pinned it. Requires a Bearer token and membership in the room.

Performs a full-text search across all chat messages the authenticated user has access to. The `query` query parameter specifies the search term. Supports optional filtering by `roomId` to scope the search to a specific room. Returns a paginated list of matching messages, each including the message content, sender, room ID, and timestamp. Requires a Bearer token.

Retrieves all media files (images, videos, audio, documents) shared in a specific chat room. The `roomId` path variable identifies the room. Supports pagination via `page` and `limit` query parameters, and optional filtering by `type` (e.g., `image`, `video`). Returns an array of media objects, each including the file URL, uploader, MIME type, and upload timestamp. Requires a Bearer token and membership in the room.

Returns aggregate statistics for a specific chat room. The `roomId` path variable identifies the room. The response includes metrics such as total message count, total media files shared, number of members, and the date the room was created. Useful for admin dashboards and analytics. Requires a Bearer token and membership in the room.

item.description: The **Chat** folder covers all real-time messaging functionality on the Ding platform. It includes endpoints for creating and managing chat rooms (both direct one-on-one and group rooms), sending and receiving text and media messages, managing room members and their roles, reacting to messages with emoji, tracking read receipts and unread counts, pinning important messages, searching message history, and browsing room media galleries. These endpoints are used by the Ding mobile and web clients to power the full in-app messaging experience. All endpoints require a valid Bearer token, and most require the authenticated user to be a member of the relevant room.

item.name: Noro

request.description: Sends a text message to the Noro AI assistant and receives a conversational reply. The request body must include `message` (string) — the user's input text. Noro processes the message and returns a contextual AI-generated response. Requires a Bearer token. Returns the assistant's reply text along with a timestamp and session metadata.

response.body: {"data":{"reply":"I'm sorry to hear you've been feeling stressed. It's completely normal to feel that way sometimes. A few things that might help: try taking short breaks throughout your day, practice deep breathing, and make sure you're getting enough sleep. Would you like to talk more about what's been on your mind?","sessionId":"session_noro_a1b2c3","respondedAt":"2024-06-02T12:00:00Z"}}

request.description: Retrieves the authenticated user's full conversation history with the Noro AI assistant. Returns a chronological list of message objects, each including the role (`user` or `assistant`), the message content, and the timestamp. Supports pagination via `page` and `limit` query parameters. Requires a Bearer token.

Work pressure can be exhausting. Have you been able to set any boundaries around your working hours?","timestamp":"2024-06-02T12:01:05Z"}],"pagination":{"page":1,"limit":20,"total":4}}}

request.description: Uploads an audio file to be transcribed into text by the Noro AI. The request body must be sent as `multipart/form-data` with the audio file attached under the `audio` field. Supported formats include MP3, WAV, and M4A. Returns the transcribed text string along with the detected language and confidence score. Requires a Bearer token.

response.name: Success - 200
response.body: {"data":{"transcription":"Hey Noro, I've been feeling a bit anxious today and I just wanted to talk to someone.","language":"en","confidence":0.97,"durationSeconds":5.2}}

request.description: Converts a text string into synthesized speech audio using the Noro AI text-to-speech engine. The request body must include `text` (string) — the content to be spoken. Optional parameters include `voice` (e.g., `female`, `male`) and `language` (e.g., `en`, `es`). Returns a URL to the generated audio file or a binary audio stream. Requires a Bearer token.

item.description: The **Noro** folder covers the original version of Ding's AI assistant feature. Noro is a conversational AI companion that users can chat with directly. This folder includes endpoints for sending a text message to Noro and receiving a reply, retrieving the user's full conversation history with the assistant, uploading audio for speech-to-text transcription, and converting text to synthesized speech audio. These endpoints are used by the Ding app to power the Noro chat interface, voice input, and audio playback features. All endpoints require a valid Bearer token.

item.name: Moderation

request.description: Submits a moderation report against a piece of content (post, comment, message, or user). The request body must include `targetId` (string) — the ID of the reported entity, `targetType` (string, e.g., `post`, `comment`, `user`), and `reason` (string, e.g., `spam`, `harassment`, `hate_speech`). An optional `description` field can provide additional context. Requires a Bearer token. Returns the created report object with a unique report ID and status `pending`.

response.name: Created - 201
response.body: {"data":{"id":"report_r1s2t3","targetId":"post_abc123","targetType":"POST","reason":"SPAM","description":"This post contains repeated promotional links with no relevant content.","reportedBy":"user_abc123","status":"PENDING","createdAt":"2024-06-02T13:00:00Z"}}

request.description: Returns a paginated list of all moderation reports submitted on the platform. Supports filtering by `status` (e.g., `pending`, `dismissed`, `actioned`) and `targetType` (e.g., `post`, `user`) via query parameters. Each report object includes the reporter's user ID, the reported entity, the reason, and the current status. Requires an admin-level Bearer token.

Dismisses a specific moderation report, marking it as reviewed and no action taken. The `commentId` path variable identifies the report to dismiss. Typically used when the reported content does not violate community guidelines. Requires an admin-level Bearer token. Returns the updated report object with status set to `dismissed`.

Bans a user from the platform, preventing them from logging in or interacting with any content. The `targetUserId` path variable identifies the user to ban. The optional request body can include `reason` (string) and `durationDays` (integer, omit for a permanent ban). Requires an admin-level Bearer token. Returns the ban record with the ban ID, target user, issuing admin, reason, and expiry date.

response.name: Created - 201
response.body: {"data":{"banId":"ban_b1c2d3","targetUserId":"user_xyz789","targetUsername":"janedoe","issuedBy":"admin_mod001","reason":"Repeated harassment of other users after prior warnings.","durationDays":30,"expiresAt":"2024-07-02T14:00:00Z","createdAt":"2024-06-02T14:00:00Z"}}

item.description: The **Moderation** folder contains endpoints for reporting and actioning user-generated content that violates Ding's community guidelines. Any authenticated user can submit a report against a post, comment, message, or another user. Platform administrators can then review the queue of pending reports, dismiss reports that don't require action, and ban users who have violated the platform's terms of service. These endpoints are used by the Ding moderation dashboard and the in-app reporting flow. User-facing report submission requires a standard Bearer token, while review and enforcement actions require an admin-level token.

item.name: Marketplace Public

request.description: Returns a paginated list of all active marketplace products. Supports `page` and `limit` query parameters for pagination. No authentication is required. Each product object includes its ID, title, price, currency, seller info, and thumbnail image. Use this endpoint to power the marketplace browse/search page.

request.description: Initiates a purchase of the product identified by the `productId` path variable. Requires a valid user Bearer token (`{{userToken}}`). On success (HTTP 201), returns a transaction object whose `id` is automatically stored in the `transactionId` collection variable for use in subsequent requests. The response includes the transaction ID, status, product snapshot, buyer info, and total amount charged.

item.description: The **Marketplace Public** folder contains endpoints accessible to any user on the Ding platform, including unauthenticated visitors. These endpoints power the buyer-facing side of the marketplace: browsing the product catalogue, viewing individual product details, and initiating a purchase. The buy endpoint requires a valid user Bearer token, while listing and viewing products are open to all. Use these endpoints to build product discovery and checkout flows.

item.name: Marketplace Seller

request.description: Submits a new seller application for the authenticated user. The request body is `multipart/form-data` and must include personal details (full name, phone, email, address), identity verification fields (ID card number, front/back images, face photo), and banking information (commercial registration number, bank account number, card details). Requires a user Bearer token. On success (HTTP 201), the new application's `id` is stored in the `applicationId` collection variable.

Returns the current status of the authenticated user's seller application. Requires a user Bearer token. The response includes the application status (`pending`, `approved`, or `declined`), submission timestamp, and any rejection reason if the application was declined. Use this endpoint to show applicants their onboarding progress.

Retrieves the full seller profile for the authenticated seller. Requires a seller-level Bearer token (`{{sellerToken}}`). Returns the seller's business name, contact details, city, country, bank account info (masked), rating, total sales count, and account status. Use this to populate the seller dashboard profile page.

Partially updates the authenticated seller's profile. Requires a seller-level Bearer token (`{{sellerToken}}`). Accepts a JSON body with any subset of updatable fields: `businessName`, `phoneNumber`, `city`, and similar profile fields. Returns the full updated seller profile object on success.

Creates a new product listing in the marketplace on behalf of the authenticated seller. Requires a seller-level Bearer token (`{{sellerToken}}`). The JSON body must include `title`, `description`, `price`, `currency`, `quantity`, and an `images` array of URLs. On success (HTTP 201), the new product's `id` is stored in the `productId` collection variable.

Partially updates an existing product listing identified by the `productId` path variable. Requires a seller-level Bearer token (`{{sellerToken}}`). Accepts a JSON body with any subset of updatable fields such as `price`, `quantity`, `title`, or `description`. Returns the full updated product object on success. Only the seller who owns the product may update it.

Permanently deletes the product listing identified by the `productId` path variable. Requires a seller-level Bearer token (`{{sellerToken}}`). Only the seller who owns the product may delete it. Returns HTTP 200 with a success message on completion. Products with active or pending transactions cannot be deleted.

Returns a paginated list of all product listings belonging to the authenticated seller. Requires a seller-level Bearer token (`{{sellerToken}}`). Supports `page` and `limit` query parameters. Each item includes the product ID, title, price, quantity, status, and creation date. Use this to populate the seller's product management dashboard.

Returns a paginated list of the authenticated seller's currently active deals (transactions in progress). Requires a seller-level Bearer token (`{{sellerToken}}`). Supports `page` and `limit` query parameters. Each deal includes the transaction ID, buyer info, product snapshot, amount, and current status. Use this to monitor ongoing sales.

Returns a paginated history of all completed, cancelled, or otherwise resolved deals for the authenticated seller. Requires a seller-level Bearer token (`{{sellerToken}}`). Supports `page` and `limit` query parameters. Each record includes the transaction ID, product, buyer, final amount, resolution status, and timestamps. Use this for earnings reporting and dispute reference.

item.description: The **Marketplace Seller** folder contains endpoints used by approved sellers to manage their presence on the Ding marketplace. Sellers can apply for a seller account (with identity and banking documents), check their application status, view and update their seller profile, create and manage product listings, and review their active deals and deal history. All endpoints require a valid seller-level Bearer token (`{{sellerToken}}`), except the application endpoints which use a regular user token.

item.name: Marketplace Admin

request.description: Returns a paginated list of seller applications currently awaiting admin review. Requires an admin-level Bearer token (`{{adminToken}}`). Supports `page` and `limit` query parameters. Each application record includes the applicant's name, email, submission date, and current status. Use this as the starting point for the admin seller-onboarding review workflow.

Retrieves the full details of a specific seller application identified by the `applicationId` path variable. Requires an admin-level Bearer token (`{{adminToken}}`). Returns all submitted fields including personal info, identity document image URLs, banking details, and the current review status. Use this to inspect an application before approving or declining it.

Approves the seller application identified by the `applicationId` path variable, granting the applicant seller-level access on the platform. Requires an admin-level Bearer token (`{{adminToken}}`). No request body is needed. Returns the updated application object with status set to `approved` and the timestamp of the decision.

Declines the seller application identified by the `applicationId` path variable. Requires an admin-level Bearer token (`{{adminToken}}`). The JSON body must include a `reason` string explaining why the application was rejected; this reason is surfaced to the applicant. Returns the updated application object with status set to `declined`.

request.description: Returns a paginated list of all approved sellers on the platform. Requires an admin-level Bearer token (`{{adminToken}}`). Supports `page` and `limit` query parameters. Each seller record includes their user ID, business name, status (active, suspended, banned), total sales, and registration date. Use this as the main seller management view for admins.

Retrieves the full seller profile for the seller identified by the `sellerUserId` path variable. Requires an admin-level Bearer token (`{{adminToken}}`). Returns all seller profile fields including business name, contact info, banking details (masked), account status, total sales, and any enforcement history. Use this before taking moderation actions.

Permanently bans the seller identified by the `sellerUserId` path variable, revoking their seller access and hiding their listings. Requires an admin-level Bearer token (`{{adminToken}}`). The JSON body must include a `cause` string documenting the reason for the ban. Returns the updated seller record with status set to `banned`.

Lifts an existing ban on the seller identified by the `sellerUserId` path variable, restoring their seller access and making their listings visible again. Requires an admin-level Bearer token (`{{adminToken}}`). No request body is needed. Returns the updated seller record with status set to `active`.

Temporarily suspends the seller identified by the `sellerUserId` path variable, preventing them from making new sales while a review is in progress. Requires an admin-level Bearer token (`{{adminToken}}`). The JSON body must include a `cause` string. Existing active deals are not cancelled. Returns the updated seller record with status set to `suspended`.

Lifts an active suspension on the seller identified by the `sellerUserId` path variable, restoring their ability to sell on the platform. Requires an admin-level Bearer token (`{{adminToken}}`). No request body is needed. Returns the updated seller record with status set to `active`.

Cancels the transaction identified by the `transactionId` path variable. Requires an admin-level Bearer token (`{{adminToken}}`). The JSON body must include a `cause` string explaining the reason for cancellation (e.g., payment dispute, fraud). Returns the updated transaction record with status set to `cancelled` and the cancellation timestamp.

Returns a paginated audit log of all significant marketplace admin actions (approvals, declines, bans, suspensions, cancellations). Requires an admin-level Bearer token (`{{adminToken}}`). Supports `page` and `limit` query parameters. Each log entry includes the action type, target entity, acting admin ID, and timestamp. Use this for compliance, accountability, and debugging.

item.description: The **Marketplace Admin** folder contains privileged endpoints used by Ding platform administrators to oversee and moderate the marketplace. Admins can review and act on seller applications (approve or decline), list and inspect active sellers, take enforcement actions (ban, unban, suspend, unsuspend), cancel disputed transactions, and retrieve audit logs of all marketplace activity. All endpoints require an admin-level Bearer token (`{{adminToken}}`).

item.name: Calls (Sprint 16)

request.description: Returns the current screen-sharing state for a call in the specified room. The `roomId` path variable identifies the room. The response indicates whether screen sharing is currently active, which participant is sharing, and the stream ID. Useful for syncing UI state when a new participant joins an ongoing call. Requires a Bearer token and membership in the room.

Retrieves a list of call quality hints for an active or recent call session in the specified room. The `roomId` path variable identifies the room. Quality hints include suggested actions such as reducing video resolution, disabling video, or switching network. Returns an array of hint objects, each with a `type`, `severity`, and `message`. item.description: The **Calls (Sprint 16)** folder covers real-time audio and video calling features on the Ding platform. It provides endpoints for retrieving the current screen-sharing state of an active call in a room, and for fetching call quality hints that help the client adapt to poor network conditions (e.g., reducing video resolution or switching to audio-only mode). These endpoints are used by the Ding calling UI to synchronize participant state and deliver a smooth call experience. All endpoints require a valid Bearer token and active membership in the relevant room.

item.name: Noro V2 (Sprint 16)

request.description: Creates a new persistent conversation thread with the Noro V2 AI assistant. The request body can include an optional `title` (string) to label the conversation. Returns the newly created conversation object with a unique `conversationId`, title, creation timestamp, and initial status. Requires a Bearer token. The returned `conversationId` is used in subsequent requests to add messages and retrieve history.

Returns a paginated list of all Noro V2 conversation threads belonging to the authenticated user. Supports `limit` and `cursor` query parameters for pagination. Each conversation object includes the `conversationId`, title, message count, and the timestamp of the last message. Requires a Bearer token.

Sends a new user message to a specific Noro V2 conversation and receives the AI assistant's reply. The `conversationId` path variable identifies the conversation. The request body must include `content` (string) — the user's message text. Returns the assistant's response message object, including the AI-generated `content`, `role`, and `createdAt` timestamp. Requires a Bearer token and ownership of the conversation.

item.description: The **Noro V2 (Sprint 16)** folder covers the upgraded version of Ding's AI assistant, introducing persistent multi-turn conversation threads. Unlike the original Noro, V2 organizes interactions into named conversations that can be created, listed, browsed, and deleted. It also introduces crisis detection capabilities — when the AI identifies signs of mental health distress in a conversation, the platform can report the crisis event, log intervention actions taken, and surface relevant emergency hotlines. These endpoints are used by the Ding app's Noro V2 chat interface and the platform's safety and wellbeing systems. Most endpoints require a valid Bearer token.

item.name: Reels (Sprint 17)

request.description: Requests a pre-signed upload URL for a new reel video file. The client should upload the raw video directly to the returned URL (e.g., an S3 pre-signed URL) and then call the Finalize Reel endpoint with the resulting storage key. Requires a Bearer token via the `Authorization` header. On success, the response includes the `reelId` (stored automatically in the `reelId` collection variable) and the pre-signed upload URL.

Finalizes a reel after the raw video has been uploaded to storage. The `reelId` path variable identifies the reel created in the upload-URL step. The JSON body must include `rawVideoKey` (the storage key of the uploaded file), `caption`, `hashtags` array, `durationSec`, `width`, and `height`. Requires a Bearer token. On success, the reel is queued for processing and becomes visible in the feed once transcoding is complete.

Returns the current processing status of the reel identified by the `reelId` path variable. Requires a Bearer token. Possible statuses include `pending`, `processing`, `ready`, and `failed`. Use this endpoint to poll for completion after calling Finalize Reel, before showing the reel to the user.

Returns a personalised feed of reels for the authenticated user. Requires a Bearer token via the `Authorization` header. Accepts a `limit` query parameter (default 10) to control how many reels are returned per request. Each reel object includes the video URL, thumbnail, caption, hashtags, like count, comment count, and creator info. The feed is ranked by the recommendation algorithm using watch history and engagement signals.

Toggles the like status of the reel identified by the `reelId` path variable for the authenticated user. Returns a list of comments for the reel identified by the `reelId` path variable. Accepts a `limit` query parameter to control the number of comments returned. item.description: The **Reels (Sprint 17)** folder contains endpoints for Ding's short-form video feature. The upload flow is two-step: first request a pre-signed upload URL, then finalize the reel after the video file has been uploaded to storage. Once published, reels appear in the personalised feed and can be viewed, liked, commented on, shared, and deleted. View tracking (watch percentage) is also supported to power the recommendation algorithm. Most endpoints require a Bearer token via the `Authorization` header.

item.name: Audio Tracks (Sprint 17)

request.description: Returns the full catalogue of available audio tracks that can be attached to reels or posts. No authentication is required. Each track object includes its ID, title, artist name, duration in seconds, genre, cover art URL, and audio file URL. On success, the first track's `id` is automatically stored in the `audioTrackId` collection variable.

Returns a curated list of currently trending audio tracks, ranked by recent usage count across reels and posts. No authentication is required. Each track object includes its ID, title, artist, duration, genre, cover art URL, audio file URL, and current usage count. Use this to populate a "Trending Sounds" section in the content creation UI.

Retrieves the full details of the audio track identified by the `audioTrackId` path variable. No authentication is required. Returns the track's title, artist, duration, genre, BPM, cover art URL, audio file URL, total usage count, and upload date. Use this to display track details before a user attaches it to their content.

Registers that the authenticated user has used the audio track identified by the `audioTrackId` path variable in a piece of content. Requires a Bearer token via the `Authorization` header. This increments the track's usage counter, which feeds the trending algorithm. Returns the updated usage count for the track.

item.description: The **Audio Tracks (Sprint 17)** folder contains endpoints for managing the library of background music and audio tracks that users can attach to their reels or posts. Endpoints allow browsing the full catalogue, discovering trending tracks, fetching a specific track by ID, and registering that a track has been used in a piece of content (which increments its usage counter and feeds the trending algorithm). Authentication is required only for the "use" registration endpoint.
